Since OpenAI launched the first GPT-5 models for ChatGPT, it has been just over a year. Now it is GPT-6 Astra's turn to upgrade the features of ChatGPT and Codex. Details are as follows.

GPT-6 Astra Details

OpenAI officially announced its new model GPT-6 Astra, calling it "the world's smartest and most aligned model".

Here is more content from today's official announcement:

OpenAI further explained how GPT-6 enhances computer operation capabilities, that is, letting ChatGPT use your Mac or other desktop computers, including running in the background while you work:

OpenAI also stated that GPT-6 Astra is "the most suitable model for software engineering to date".

As for Codex, what's new in GPT-6:

OpenAI called GPT-6 Astra a "major leap in cybersecurity capabilities", and pointed out that it "reached the Critical threshold for cybersecurity in our Preparedness Framework".

For this reason, the model will be gradually opened to users.

OpenAI stated: "GPT‑6 Astra will be launched to a limited number of organisations starting today, and will be opened to all ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users in the coming days. It will also be available via the OpenAI API and AWS."

"Astra's usage will count towards existing subscription quotas—users and businesses can also purchase additional usage credits. Users on Pro, Business, and Enterprise plans can also use GPT‑6 Astra Pro. Enterprise administrators can enable Astra for their workspaces; rollout is off by default."

The Road to GPT-6 Astra

GPT-5 was launched on August 7, 2025, replacing GPT-4o and multiple reasoning models to become the default model for ChatGPT. Its core feature is automatic routing: ChatGPT can choose to answer immediately or initiate deeper reasoning based on the content of the request. OpenAI also claimed that GPT-5 had fewer factual errors than GPT-4o.

Apple adopted this model in iOS 26, iPadOS 26, and macOS Tahoe 26. ChatGPT requests delivered through Apple Intelligence, including Siri handoffs, Writing Tools, and Image Intelligence, have switched from GPT-4o to GPT-5.

The November GPT-5.1 promised warmer, more natural responses. The December "code red" GPT-5.2 accelerated professional work to counter Gemini. GPT-5.3 Instant improved ChatGPT's "awkward" tone, and two days later GPT-5.4 Thinking was launched with a 1-million token context window and built-in computer operation capabilities.

OpenAI subsequently added GPT-5.4 mini and nano, the limited GPT-5.4-Cyber, GPT-5.5 for higher-autonomy tasks, GPT-5.5 Instant, and the GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna models launched in July.

From the Codex Mac App to the New ChatGPT

The software surrounding these models has also changed. OpenAI launched a dedicated Codex Mac App in February, serving as a hub for running multiple coding agents, reviewing changes, and scheduling work.

In July, Codex essentially became the new ChatGPT desktop application, merging Chat, Work, and Codex into one, while the original native client was renamed ChatGPT Classic.

For me, Codex has changed the way I collaborate with ChatGPT the most. I can outsource more work that doesn't require deep thinking to it, and even build tools on the Mac that I couldn't have built on my own.

GPT-6 Availability

OpenAI stated that the new GPT-6 model will initially only be available to members of its cybersecurity-focused Daybreak programme. This is similar to the rollout pace of the previous GPT-5.6.
